title: relay_client.rs: MAIL FROM address sanitization strips only CR/LF but not angle brackets and other injection chars
description: relay_client.rs run_smtp_session line 239: safe_from = envelope.mail_from.replace(['\r', '\n'], ""). This is interpolated as MAIL FROM:<{safe_from}>. RCPT TO has additional validation to reject < and > in the address (line 258), but MAIL FROM only strips CR/LF. A mail_from value containing '>' would prematurely close the angle bracket and allow SMTP command injection in the MAIL FROM line. Example: mail_from = 'x@y.com> BODY=8BITMIME' would produce 'MAIL FROM:<x@y.com> BODY=8BITMIME>' which is valid ESMTP syntax that injects an extension parameter. Worse, 'x@y.com>\r\nRCPT TO:<evil@example.com>' would inject a new command, though the replace already strips CR/LF. The < and > check from RCPT TO should also be applied to MAIL FROM.
